current_sprint.title: Foundation, safety and de-risking
current_sprint.goal: Make the repository trustworthy as the source of truth, remove the credential leak risk, and run the three blocking hardware experiments that determine whether the product's headline features are feasible at all.

progress.note: Generated by scripts/project-tracker/render.py. Do not hand-edit.

honest_status.summary: Hardware capabilities are substantially proven and the product has now started to build on them. The decisive gap that was open at the last update is closed: PPP over UART now negotiates end to end on the Airtel SIM, giving the ESP32 a real IP interface (100.76.140.112, gw 10.64.64.64). That was the single precondition gating the NAT router. What is still unproven is product behaviour, not hardware: end-to-end MQTT publish, any forwarding/NAT, and any web portal.
verified_and_usable: GNSS fix: 18.480776, 73.897998 in 69 s cold start (PWRKEY power-on sequence is mandatory; see L-1)
Cellular LBS fallback: +CLBS: 0,18.481703,73.897415,550, corroborated against the GNSS fix

PPP over UART: lwIP reaches phase RUNNING, local=100.76.140.112 gateway=10.64.64.64 mtu=1500, held stable, reproduced on a cold boot. Three fixes were needed (BUG-006): post-CONNECT settle delay, tcpip_init(), and the core lock.
Camera OV2640 live capture, SD card round trip (Arduino), outbound SMS, outgoing call control
not_yet_proven: End-to-end MQTT publish from the device to the broker (TASK-405, TEST-403 FAIL)
IP forwarding / NAT between SoftAP clients and the LTE link, and the 3 s dual-WAN failover target (REQ-004). The PPP interface it needs now exists; the routing above it does not.
Audio hardware presence (RISK-003) - needs physical board inspection, still blocking for voice/ESP-SR
honest_status.immediate_risk: RESOLVED in code, still open as a human action. The hardcoded broker credential in the tracker sketch has been removed and a secrets scan over the full git history is clean, but removal is not rotation: the exposed HiveMQ credential must still be rotated at the broker (TASK-004, RISK-008). Separately, the negotiated PPP address is carrier-grade NAT (100.x.x.x), so the LTE leg is outbound-only and cannot accept inbound connections - that constrains the REQ-004 design.

next_action: Close ADR-005 now that TASK-020 is done, since the PPP outcome was one of its two stated preconditions. RISK-002 is retired, so the remaining question is RISK-003 (audio hardware), which needs a physical look at the board. In parallel, TASK-405 (MQTT CIPSEND/CONNACK) is now unblocked by nothing and gates the first real end-to-end device-to-broker publish. The user has two physical actions outstanding: rotate the broker credential, and confirm whether the board has I2S mic and amp populated.
